display.purpose: Site mark and article h2 (19px). True display work is ASCII block art, not large type.

body.purpose: All interface text in Departure Mono: nav, command headings, listings, windows, footer.

article.purpose: Long-form prose in Iosevka at 1.65 line-height, 72ch measure. The one place the site breathes.

label.purpose: Asides, dates, reading times, tags, captions. Always in Comment.

code.purpose: Code blocks, window bodies, ASCII figures. Iosevka 14px.

motion.name: hard-cut
motion.purpose: Interactive states never transition; instant repaint by doctrine.

motion.name: screen-repaint
motion.purpose: Page navigation. The incoming screen is painted over the outgoing one top-down in discrete steps, like a terminal redraw. Never eased.

components.name: Command Heading
components.description: The section-heading grammar of the whole site: green $, command in Base, argument in Accent, and live stats pulled right by a dotted leader.
components.html: ls -la~/writing3 posts · 9.4k words
components.css: .ds-cmd { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: 2px 8px; margin: 40px 0 10px; font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); } .ds-cmd::before { content: "$" / ""; color: var(--green, #4fd67f); } .ds-cmd-flag { color: var(--accent, #eb242a); } .ds-cmd-aside { display: flex; flex: 1; align-items: baseline; gap: 10px; color: var(--comment, #a39694); font-size: 14px; } .ds-cmd-aside::before { content: ""; flex: 1; min-width: 24px; align-self: center; border-bottom: 1px dotted var(--rule, #50171c); }

components.name: Output Block
components.description: The only sanctioned container: a 1px Rule spine with a 16px indent. Everything that follows a command is its output.
components.html: Everything that follows a command is its output. Prose runs in Iosevka at a 72ch measure; there are no cards on this site.
components.css: .ds-out { padding-left: 16px; border-left: 1px solid var(--rule, #50171c); } .ds-out p { margin: 0; max-width: 72ch; font-family: "Iosevka", monospace; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.65; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); }

components.name: Inline Link
components.description: Underlined Base; hover and focus invert fully. Focus adds the 2px Blood outline.
components.html: Read the home-server writeup for details.
components.css: .ds-linkline { margin: 0; font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; font-size: 15px; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); } .ds-link { color: var(--base, #ece4e2); text-decoration: underline; } .ds-link:hover, .ds-link:focus-visible { color: var(--bg, #0a0507); background: var(--base, #ece4e2); } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blood, #db001a); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Bracketed labels between two hairlines; current page and hover are full inversions. No theme control: the site is dark, full stop.
components.html: [ ~/ ][ blog ][ projects ][ uses ]
components.css: .ds-menu { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 2px 10px; padding: 12px 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule, #50171c); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #50171c); font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; font-size: 15px; } .ds-menu-a { padding: 3px 0; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-menu-a[aria-current="page"], .ds-menu-a:hover, .ds-menu-a:focus-visible { color: var(--bg, #0a0507); background: var(--base, #ece4e2); }

components.name: Listing Row
components.description: Baseline grid of date / underlined title / meta; hovering fills the title with Blood.
components.html: 2024-12-24Static analysis of RansomHub's ESXi locker14 min
components.css: .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 105px minmax(0, 1fr) auto; gap: 0 12px; align-items: baseline; padding-bottom: 4px; font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; font-size: 15px; text-decoration: none; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); } .ds-row-when, .ds-row-len { color: var(--comment, #a39694); } .ds-row-title { color: var(--base, #ece4e2); text-decoration: underline; padding: 4px; } .ds-row:hover .ds-row-title, .ds-row:focus-visible .ds-row-title { color: var(--bg, #0a0507); background: var(--accent, #eb242a); text-decoration: none; }

components.name: Floating Window
components.description: Signature component: red-chromed window with a draggable title bar and a prompt-led pre body. Degrades to a static aside without JS.
components.html:
status
$ ./status

host....... lacorte.city
build...... 3734d1e
updated.... 2026-08-04
components.css: .ds-window { width: min(340px, 100%); border: 1px solid var(--win-line, #5f171e); background: var(--bg, #0a0507); font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; } .ds-window-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; min-height: 26px; padding: 4px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--win-edge, #8d1622); background: var(--win-bar, #1a0a0e); color: var(--win-title, #f2252b); font-size: 15px; line-height: 1; cursor: grab; } .ds-window-x { width: 24px; height: 24px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid var(--win-line, #5f171e); background: transparent; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); font: inherit; font-size: 11px; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; } .ds-window-x:hover, .ds-window-x:focus-visible { color: var(--bg, #0a0507); background: var(--base, #ece4e2); } .ds-window-body { margin: 0; padding: 10px 12px; overflow-x: auto; white-space: pre; font-family: "Iosevka", monospace; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); } .ds-prompt { color: var(--green, #4fd67f); }

components.name: Taskbar
components.description: Fixed bottom strip of bordered toggle buttons; pressed state is a full inversion.
components.css: .ds-taskbar { display: flex; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 10px; border-top: 1px solid var(--win-edge, #8d1622); background: var(--win-bar, #1a0a0e); } .ds-task { min-height: 24px; padding: 2px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--win-line, #5f171e); background: transparent; color: var(--base, #ece4e2); font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-task[aria-pressed="true"], .ds-task:hover, .ds-task:focus-visible { color: var(--bg, #0a0507); background: var(--base, #ece4e2); }

components.description: Hairline-left aside with a textual `! label` colored by severity (Comment / Amber / Blood). No fills, no icons.

components.name: Code Block
components.description: Code panel with a tracked-caps header bar (the site's only tracked-caps moment) and a copy button that fills Blood on hover.
components.css: .ds-codewrap { background: var(--code-panel, #160606); } .ds-codebar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; padding: 4px 10px; color: var(--comment, #a39694); font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-codecopy { min-height: 24px; padding: 0 8px; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--comment, #a39694); font: inherit; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-codecopy:hover, .ds-codecopy:focus-visible { background: var(--accent, #eb242a); color: var(--bg, #0a0507); } .ds-pre { margin: 0; padding: 14px; background: var(--code-surface, #0c0505); overflow-x: auto; font-family: "Iosevka", monospace; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.55; color: #f5eee8; }

components.name: Tag
components.description: Plain-text chip: Comment text with a Blood # prefix. No borders, no pills.
components.css: .ds-tags { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px 1ch; margin: 0; } .ds-tag { color: var(--comment, #a39694); font-family: "Departure Mono", monospace; font-size: 14px; } .ds-tag::before { content: "#"; color: var(--accent, #eb242a); }

narrative.overview:
This is the bench where machines get taken apart and the findings get written down. Everything on the site is presented as evidence of work performed: pages open with a shell command ($ whoami, ls -la ~/writing), content arrives as that command's output, and live facts (commit hash, word counts, build date) come from the actual deploy. The mood is three things at once, deliberately held in tension: dry workshop honesty as the baseline register, blood-red menace as the visual signature (a near-black soaked in red, the quiet dread of a machine that knows too much), and personal-web warmth as the human layer — 88x31 badges, a webring, ASCII block letters, hand-labeled everything.

The system is dense and single-columned (984px max, 16px gutters), set entirely in two monospace voices, and refuses ornament: no rounded corners, no shadows, no gradients, no transitions. Depth is drawn with 1px hairlines and window chrome; interaction is an instant repaint. Per PRODUCT.md, it explicitly rejects the corporate dev-portfolio, Hollywood hacker kitsch, the sanitized minimal blog, and the heavy JS showpiece. The terminal here is real, not costume: every metaphor (windows, taskbar, prompts) behaves like the real thing and degrades to honest static HTML with JavaScript off.
keyCharacteristics: Terminal-native: content framed as command + output, everywhere
Blood-soaked dark palette (red-cast neutrals, never gray) with a full light theme and a monochrome print theme
Two monospace voices: Departure Mono (machine chrome) and Iosevka (the written word)
Flat, sharp, instant: 0px radius, no shadows, no tweens
Old-web artifacts worn sincerely: pixel icons, 88x31 badges, ASCII art, webring
Bilingual (EN / PT-BR) and no-JS resilient by doctrine

rules.name: The Soaked Neutrals Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries the red. Backgrounds, rules, window chrome, and code surfaces are all red-cast blacks (or warm plasters in light theme) — a plain gray anywhere is a bug. The menace lives in the neutrals, not in how much red is painted on top.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: Interactive state is a full color inversion: base-on-bg becomes bg-on-base (or bg-on-blood for emphasis). Never an opacity fade, never a tint, never a color-mix. Selection, nav, links, buttons, and window controls all obey it.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: --blood draws, --accent speaks. If red touches a glyph, as ink or as the fill behind one, it is --accent; contrast is symmetric, so the same token serves both directions. --blood is only for borders, rings, and chrome, which answer to 3:1 rather than 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Visible Markdown Rule
rules.body: Structure is denoted, not sized. Headings keep their literal markdown markers (##, ###) rendered in Blood; the scale barely moves, and the markers plus hairline underlines do the work. Do not introduce large display sizes to create hierarchy.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Departure Mono speaks for the machine (chrome, commands, navigation); Iosevka speaks for the human (articles, code, ASCII drawings). Never swap their roles, never add a third voice.

rules.name: The Drawn-Depth Rule
rules.body: If something must read as 'above', give it a border and a bar, never a shadow, never a blur. If it can't earn window chrome, it isn't above.

rules.name: The Hard Cut Rule
rules.body: No CSS transitions or keyframe animations on interactive states: hover, focus, open, and close are instant repaints. The only motion on the site is physical (the user dragging a window) and the page repaint on navigation, and prefers-reduced-motion flattens both.

rules.name: The Power-Off Rule
rules.body: Every interactive component ships its no-JS form: windows become static asides, code blocks render plain with no copy button, and the single dark theme needs no negotiation at all. If a proposed component has no honest power-off state, it does not ship.

rules.name: The Screen Repaint Rule
rules.body: Pages never dissolve into one another. On navigation the outgoing screen holds still and the incoming one is painted straight over it from the top down, in eight discrete steps across 140ms (clip-path plus steps(), mix-blend-mode: normal so the two overwrite instead of blending). It must stay a step function: an eased wipe is just a fade wearing a costume. Reduced motion drops it to a plain cut.

rules.name: The Real Command Rule
rules.body: A command heading names the command that would actually produce the output beneath it. ./status prints a real build hash, so the rest holds to the same standard: the changelog is headed git log --date=short --format="%ad %s" rather than --oneline, because --oneline prints abbreviated hashes and that section prints dates and subjects.

dos: Do frame new content as command + output: a Cmd heading ($ verb ~/object) followed by an .out block. That grammar is the site.
Do use full inversion for every interactive state — exact pairs only: Base↔Bg, or Bg-on-Blood for emphasis.
Do keep every corner 0px, every border 1px, every surface shadowless.
Do keep neutrals soaked: new darks mix from Blood (like #0c0505, #160606), never from gray.
Do ship the no-JS fallback and the reduced-motion path with the feature, not after it.
Do reach for --accent the moment red meets text, and re-measure both themes when any red changes: all 26 text pairs currently clear 4.5:1.
Do keep both locales first-class: grids use minmax(0, 1fr), rows wrap, and PT-BR strings (typically longer) must fit without truncation.
Do keep facts live: stats, dates, and build info come from the deploy, never hard-coded theater.
Do give decorative generated content empty CSS alt text (content: "## " / "") so the markers stay on screen and out of the screen reader.
Do cap any summary line at 72ch, the same measure as prose, even inside a dense list row.
donts: Don't build the corporate dev-portfolio: no hero headshot, no skill bars, no 'Hi, I'm Gabriel 👋', no card grids, no testimonial energy. There are deliberately no cards on this site — grouping is done by the Output Block spine or window chrome.
Don't do Hollywood hacker kitsch: no Matrix-green glitch text, no scanlines, no neon 'cyber' gradients, no gratuitous skull ASCII. The menace is quiet or it isn't menace.
Don't sand it into a sanitized minimal blog: no friendly rounded sans, no boundless whitespace, no reading-app chrome.
Don't ship a heavy JS showpiece: no WebGL, no scroll-jacking, no cursor trails — the site advertises a no-JS button and must deserve it.
Don't tween. No transition:, no easing curves, no fade-on-hover. The Hard Cut Rule is doctrine.
Don't round a corner, cast a shadow, or paint a gradient. Ever.
Don't introduce a proportional typeface, a third font family, or bold-weight UI text — emphasis is Blood, not weight.
Don't replace textual markers ($, ##, [+], ! note, #tag) with icons. The markers are the interface.
